_oracle_note: The injecting oracle of admission check (b): one behavioural check per defect in cwe_catalog, run with the candidate checkout as cwd so `flask` imports from the candidate. Nonzero exit means a violation was detected (expect_zero=False); the battery exits 0 when it cannot run, so a broken oracle admits nothing. It lives outside the checkout so no producer, challenger or policy can read it. Artifact-disjoint from the F2 rule sets and from flask's suite by construction: it has no patterns and reuses no test code. Covers all 10 catalog defects (tests/test_oracle.py); the regex SAST scanner the spec first proposed covers 0.
_note: PILOT, not the confirmatory study. Real agents, real producers, real decisions, but: task selection is the history fallback rather than the PR API, the salt is a pilot salt and not a freeze, there is no blinded equivalence review, and severity comes from the rubric anchors rather than from two adjudicators. Nothing here may enter the paper's RQ1 tables. corpus/flask/ stays reserved for the frozen run.
_authors_note: Authoring agents decided 2026-10-19 (setup spec D6). Both are API models through their vendor CLIs, so no API key enters the replication package; the open-weight arm of the original S4 is gone and the deviation is recorded in the spec. Shell capability is deliberately symmetric: codex's workspace-write sandbox permits model-generated shell, so claude carries Bash, and the mode factor contrasts vendors rather than tool access. Model IDs are pinned here rather than taken from local CLI config; the served weights behind an ID are not pinnable, which is a reproducibility limit to state in the paper.
